messages:
ashok: Seeing ~33% of new edge pod IPs deregistered from ALB target group in ap-southeast-2 right after the 10:03 HPA scale. Marked unhealthy due to healthcheck timeouts.

sara: Only ap-southeast-2? Any node or kubelet events around the scale?

ashok: Yes 957 rolling kubelet restart on a subset of nodes. HPA scaled 4 -> 12 at 10:03 and a bunch of pods landed on those nodes; readiness failed within seconds.

maria: Current config snippets pasted: 
```
ALB health check: IntervalSeconds=10, TimeoutSeconds=5, HealthyThreshold=2, Path=/healthz

readinessProbe:
  initialDelaySeconds: 2
  periodSeconds: 5
  timeoutSeconds: 1
  failureThreshold: 3
```

kevin: That readiness is really aggressive for edge pools. If kube-proxy/iptables are still reconciling, HTTP GETs will time out. ALB starts probing quickly and may deregister before pod reports Ready.

ashok: Pod logs show: 
```
GET /healthz -> net/http: request canceled (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)
```
ALB TG event: target 10.0.12.78:8080 failed health checks (timeout) -> deregistered.

maria: Immediate mitigations: bump initialDelay to 12-15s for edge deployments, bump timeout to 2s and/or period to 10s. Optionally increase ALB Interval to 15s and HealthyThreshold to 3 while we stabilize.

dev-deploy-bot: Hotfix PR #4931 deployed to canary at 10:28 (sets initialDelaySeconds=15, timeoutSeconds=2, adds 5s postStart sleep). Monitoring target-group and readiness.

kevin: Longer term: prefer TargetGroupBinding + k8s readiness gate so pods register only when Ready; add a node-level readiness check (kube-proxy/kubelet up) before allowing scheduling in edge TG. Also update probe templates for edge pools to be more conservative.

sara: Add alerting: spike in deregistrations > X/min for a TG should page infra oncall. Also add a brief runbook.

maria: I'll write runbook entry "ALB deregistrations after scale" with commands: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn> --region ap-southeast-2`, `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n edge`, `kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -n edge`.

ashok: Canary normalized after ~3 minutes. Plan: roll probe changes to prod in a controlled window tonight; if we still see flapping we'll also tweak ALB Interval/HealthyThreshold and investigate kube-proxy warmup metrics. Will follow up with postmortem.

sara: Thanks all. If anyone sees another spike, paste ALB TG events and `kubectl describe pod`, and ping #eng-infra. :thumbsup:
